messages:
tasha_pm: Drafting a playbook proposal for 'elastic headroom' in Dedicated — allows short-term headroom above reservation to avoid preemptions, with cost smoothing. Link to doc (WIP): https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated/elastic-headroom. Starting this thread for prioritization + launch criteria.

mike_infra: Love the idea. Main concerns: how we measure headroom usage and chargeback. Need telemetry plumbing and quota enforcement.

olivia_sre: From ops: evictions will likely drop but we risk noisy neighbors. Need per-tenant isolation score and a hard-cap fallback. Also define rollback triggers and observability for tail latency.

raj_sales: Customers keep asking for predictable latencies and no sudden evictions. Sales note: we can't promise unlimited headroom in contracts. We need clear guardrails & SLA language before shipping.

sophia_custsuc: Two enterprise customers (FinOpsCo, HealthChat) specifically asked for burst during peak business hours only. They want visibility in Console + alerts when headroom usage > 30%.

dustin_research: Experiment idea: 2-week A/B where 10% of Dedicated traffic gets 5–10% elastic headroom. Measure p95/p99 latencies, eviction counts, and cost delta. Instrument events: headroom_granted, headroom_revoked, eviction_prevented.

tasha_pm: Proposed launch criteria (candidate):
- Telemetry: headroom events + per-tenant usage surfaced in Console
- Safety: hard cap + automatic fallback to reserved pool within 2m if pressure spikes
- SLA wording: 'best-effort burst up to X% subject to capacity; reserved reservation still guarantees baseline throughput'
- Experiment: A/B with guardrail alerts and rollback thresholds
- Docs & billing: per-minute accounting + invoice sample
Thoughts?

mike_infra: Agree. Also need runtime flag and kernel-level batching adjustments for headroom flows — I'll add a flag `enable_headroom_flow` to the runtime; default off. Sample config for prototype:
```
headroom: {
  enabled: true,
  max_percent: 10,
  ttl_seconds: 300
}
```

olivia_sre: Ops guardrails proposed:
- If evictions > 5 across cluster in 10m => rollback headroom globally
- If p99 latency increases > 15% vs baseline => throttle headroom
We'll need runbooks, canary plan, and clear pager ownership for headroom incidents.

raj_sales: For contracts: propose two SKUs: 'Reserved + Elastic' (soft SLAs, cheaper) and 'Reserved-Protected' (no elastic, higher price). Legal will need sample wording; I'll draft and share.

sophia_custsuc: :thumbsup: Console needs: per-reservation headroom meter + an alerting rule template customers can copy. Keep UI simple — status + minutes used this billing period.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy created for branch 'elastic-headroom/proto', cluster 'staging-dedicated-3'.

tasha_pm: Next steps: Mike to estimate infra work (ETA 2w), Olivia to author runbook (ETA 1w), Raj to draft SKU & contract language (ETA 1w), Dustin to write A/B experiment spec (ETA 10d). I'll compile launch checklist and schedule a sync next Wed 10am. If no objections we'll include a Q3 roadmap slice for this.

mike_infra: ETA sounds tight but doable if we scope proto minimal (telemetry + runtime flag + safety checks). I'll open PRs.

olivia_sre: Will start runbook draft and include rollback play. cc @tasha_pm
